act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works
head: Campaign gifts were more common among sponsors of the stand-alone bills.
deck: The bills came from reports filed for Anthropic. The gifts went to committees linked to serving members.
note: The records give no link between a gift and a bill.
bridge: How much of the wider federal lobbying on AI did the network report?
source: Senate quarterly lobbying reports, Congress.gov bill records and FEC contribution filings

act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works
head: The network accounted for 0.5% of 2025 lobbying reported on federal filings naming AI.
deck: The frontier labs accounted for 6%. Each filing gives a single amount for all its issues.
note: The amounts are upper bounds on AI lobbying. A client’s in-house expenses include its fees to outside firms, which are counted once here.
bridge: How crowded was the field around state AI bills?

act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works
head: Network clients made up under 7% of the lobbying field on each state AI-safety bill examined.
deck: California and New York disclosures list network clients on all 3 bills examined. Each dot is one client per bill.
note: The disclosures identify the bills. A client’s position and the effect on a vote are outside this count.
bridge: Back in Congress, how far did lobbyists’ personal gifts reach?
source: California and New York lobbying disclosures

act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works
head: Lobbyists named for network clients reported personal gifts to 304 serving members.
deck: The broader count covers gifts made while the lobbyist’s firm was registered for a network client. The narrower count also requires the client’s filings to name the giver.
note: These are lobbyists’ own gifts to committees linked to individual members. The filing windows bound the count, and the gifts tell us nothing about a vote.
bridge: How often did people move between the Hill and these organisations?
source: Lobbyists’ semiannual contribution reports and federal lobbying registrations

act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works
head: Most documented career moves ran from the Hill to the network.
deck: The moves from Capitol Hill include positions with network organisations and their lobbying firms. Everyone moving to a congressional host in this record had a Horizon role.
note: Each career record establishes roles. It leaves the work done in those roles open.
how: Each dot is one person in that direction.
source: Congressional payroll, former posts disclosed in lobbying filings, and organisation staffing and placement records

act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works
head: Committees and a congressional commission hosted 14 of 29 Horizon placements.
deck: Horizon’s roster lists 25 fellows, including placements in members’ offices from both parties.
note: Fellows and offices choose each other. Horizon pays the stipend, and the host directs the work.
bridge: Beyond fellowships, where did the network’s research grants go?

act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works
head: Georgetown’s CSET led the grant ranking for AI and related work.
deck: The network’s funders supported AI, technology, biosecurity and catastrophic-risk work. The ranking draws on published awards and filed payments.
note: Each appearance counts a witness listed by the committee. Nothing in this record ties a grant to an appearance.
bridge: The network shows up in lobbying filings, personal gifts, career records and grants.
source: Published grant lists and IRS schedules, 2009–2026, and a House witness list
